request: Analyze GSE137631 for PMID 32409493 (Exercise-Induced Increases in Insulin Sensitivity After Bariatric Surgery Are Mediated By Muscle Extracellular Matrix Remodeling.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: Lexogen QuantSeq 3' mRNA-seq, vastus lateralis, women
final.primary_estimand: Change in skeletal-muscle gene expression from pre-surgery to 9 months after RYGB in women randomized to RYGB + combined aerobic/resistance exercise training (RYGB+ET), compared with RYGB alone (standard of care); lean women as a baseline reference
final.sample_inclusion: GEO: 6 RYGB (pre/post9), 6 RYGB+ET (pre/post9), 6 lean controls (baseline only); 3-month biopsies mentioned in abstract are not in GEO
final.repeated_measure_unit: patient (pre and post9 biopsies from the same woman)
planned_contrasts: RYGB+ET POST9 vs PRE, paired (abstract: 'candidates modulated by exercise training'; GEO summary: transcriptome changes explaining RYGB+ET improvement; DEG count not in abstract)
RYGB POST9 vs PRE, paired (surgery alone)
exercise-specific: change in RYGB+ET minus change in RYGB (randomized comparison; not stated as a DE contrast in the abstract)
POST9 groups vs lean controls (GEO summary: 'restored to a lean phenotype')

paper_threshold.source_locator: abstract does not give a DEG threshold; full text unavailable

final.paper_method: DESeq2 V1.18.1 (GEO data_processing); JMP Genomics ANOVA also listed
final.paper_results: Abstract names TGF-beta1/SMAD2/3 pathway and follistatin (FST) as exercise-modulated candidates; ECM remodeling (collagen I) reduced more with RYGB+ET. No DEG counts in abstract.

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Full text unavailable; reconstruction rests on the PubMed abstract (PMID 32409493) and GEO GSE137631 summary/overall design/data_processing. DESeq2 is named in data_processing.

checks: GEO series contact (Dantas WS, Pennington) = first author
GEO overall design matches abstract (RYGB vs RYGB+ET randomized, women, pre and 9-month muscle biopsies)
30 matrix columns map one-to-one by name to the 30 GSM titles

ownership.reasoning: GSE137631 is the paper's RNA-seq deposit; raw_counts file used (DESeq2_normalized_counts rejected as normalized input).

candidates.reason_rejected: DESeq2 size-factor-normalized, non-integer; has 33 columns incl. extra annotation; raw counts available

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns were renamed to GSM ids by prep_rename_columns.py using an explicit name rule (RYGB.k.PRE -> 'RYGB_k PRE', WD.RYGB.ET.k.T -> 'RYGB + exercise training_k T', WD.lean.control.k -> 'lean control_k'); exact index match. Subject = arm + patient number; ages agree within each PRE/POST9 pair, supporting the pairing.

final.source: GSE137631_raw_counts.txt.gz (Lexogen QuantSeq pipeline read count tables)

matrix.reasoning: integer_fraction 1.0, max 690916, file named raw_counts, data_processing: Lexogen QuantSeq pipeline read count tables then DESeq2.

design.subject: subject

final.analysis_type: paired within-arm pre/post plus between-arm change comparison
final.estimand_note: Within-arm pre/post is a surgery(+training) effect over 9 months, not an exercise effect alone; the randomized exercise effect is the difference in change between arms. Lean comparisons are associational.

design.reasoning: GEO overall design: randomized RYGB vs RYGB+ET, biopsies PRE and 9 months; lean controls baseline only. Paper used DESeq2 (within-group comparisons implied by abstract 'candidates modulated by exercise training'). The interaction (difference in change) is the only contrast isolating exercise; included as secondary. 3-month timepoint absent from GEO.

candidates.value: pooling RYGB and RYGB+ET post vs pre
candidates.reason_rejected: would mix the arms and lose the exercise contrast

covariates.name: age
covariates.disposition: not added: constant within subject, absorbed by subject blocking in paired contrasts

covariates.name: bmi
covariates.disposition: not added: outcome of surgery, post-treatment variable

covariance.reasoning: Same patient biopsied PRE and POST9 -> subject blocking. Matrix column prefix 'WD.' appears on lean and RYGB+ET columns but not on RYGB columns, which may indicate a separate processing batch per arm; any such batch is constant within subject, so within-arm paired contrasts and the difference-in-change are protected from additive batch, but lean-vs-POST comparisons crossing arms are not.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald) paired ~ subject + grp for within-arm contrasts; limma paired_change on log2(CPM+1) for difference-in-change

paper_route.reason: raw counts deposited; paper's exact DESeq2 design not stated in abstract (pairing assumed)

deviations: difference-in-change uses limma paired_change on log2(CPM+1) (no DESeq2 interaction executor with nested subject); declared deviation
lean comparisons use unpaired DESeq2 ~ grp

method.reasoning: Raw counts support DESeq2 as named in GEO data_processing.

final.deviation_note: Abstract states no DEG threshold and the full text is unavailable; workflow default BH padj < 0.05, no fold-change cutoff.

threshold.reasoning: No threshold in abstract or GEO.

caveats: Comparison with the paper rests on the abstract only (no full text); abstract gives no DEG counts.
Within-arm POST9 vs PRE confounds exercise with surgery and weight loss; exercise-specific effect = difference in change (limma, declared deviation).
Possible per-arm processing batch ('WD.' column prefix) affects lean comparisons.

study.reasoning: Abstract names FST and the TGF-beta1/SMAD2/3 pathway as exercise-modulated, and collagen I as reduced more with RYGB+ET.

discrepancies.data: GEO has PRE and POST9 only

executions.name: ET_post9_vs_pre
executions.reasoning: paired DESeq2 in RYGB+ET arm, 6 complete pairs

executions.name: exercise_x_time
executions.reasoning: randomized exercise effect: (POST9-PRE in RYGB+ET) minus (POST9-PRE in RYGB)

executions.name: ETpost_vs_LEAN
executions.reasoning: GEO summary: restoration toward lean phenotype; associational
